#+TITLE: Habits - the format, the capture template, and a test corpus

*If you are here for the format of a habit heading, or for the capture template
that writes one, it is [[*Adding a habit, and the format I always forget][the next section]].* The rest of this file is the
test corpus.

A small org directory of habits, written against <2026-09-29 Tue>, for
exercising =IsHabit()=, =HabitStreak()=, =MissedHabit()=, the agenda's habit
graph, and what =ChangeStatus= does to a repeater.

Run it without touching the real database:

#+begin_src sh
orgs -orgdir ./testdata/habits search 'IsHabit()'
orgs -orgdir ./testdata/habits search 'IsHabit() && MissedHabit()'
orgs -orgdir ./testdata/habits search 'IsHabit() && HabitStreak() >= 3' -sort Headline
orgs -orgdir ./testdata/habits agenda
#+end_src

* Adding a habit, and the format I always forget

A habit is four things, and it is only a habit if it has all of them:

1. a heading with a *live todo keyword* - TODO, NEXT, whatever the file
   declares;
2. a =SCHEDULED:= line *immediately under the headline*, carrying a *repeater*;
3. a =:STYLE: habit= property, in a drawer that is *not* at column zero;
4. a =:LOGBOOK:= of =State "DONE"= lines, which you never write yourself -
   =ChangeStatus= writes one every time the habit is ticked off, and that is
   what the streaks and the squares are read from.

Written out, with nothing in it that is optional:

#+begin_src org
  ,** TODO Morning pages
     SCHEDULED: <2026-09-30 Wed .+1d>
     :PROPERTIES:
     :STYLE:    habit
     :END:
     Ten minutes, first thing.
#+end_src

** The capture template

Paste this under =server: captureTemplates:= in =orgs.yaml=. It fills the date
in for you and asks for the one thing it cannot know, which is how often:

#+begin_src yaml
  - name: "AddHabit"
    type: "entry"
    target:
      type: "file+headline"
      filename: "habits.org"
      id: "Habits"
    template: |-
      SCHEDULED: <{{date}} {{repeat|How often? .+1d daily, .+1w/10d weekly with slack}}>
      :PROPERTIES:
      :STYLE:    habit
      :END:
      {{CONTENT}}
#+end_src

Then =c= in worg (or the pencil on the rail), pick *AddHabit*, and type the
headline with its keyword - =TODO Morning pages= - the repeater, and the body.
=orgs listcap= is how you check the yaml took.

Five things about it, each of which is a way to get a heading that looks like a
habit and is not one:

- *The keyword goes in the headline you type.* Capture writes =NewNode.Headline=
  verbatim and the template has no say in it, so =Morning pages= on its own
  gives a habit that is not a task: it will not be in an agenda and no query
  asking =IsTask()= will find it. It does still tick off - the first tick gives
  it the file's first live keyword and logs =from ""= - but that is a repair,
  not the intent.
- *=template:= is a sibling of =target:=, not a key inside it.* Indented one
  level too far it is silently a field of the target, which has no such field,
  and the template arrives empty.
- *The =|-= is load-bearing.* A yaml scalar written over several lines without a
  block scalar folds its newlines into spaces, and a property drawer on one line
  is not a property drawer.
- *The drawer must not land at column zero.* It does not, because capture
  indents every line of the content - but a habit typed by hand into a file, or
  pasted, can, and then go-org ends the headline's body at the drawer:
  =:STYLE: habit= never reaches =Headline.Properties= and the heading does not
  read as a habit at all. That is what =habits-column-zero.org= in this
  directory is for.
- *The template string is the client's, not the server's.* worg reads it and
  puts up the form; =orgs cap= does not expand it, so from a terminal you are
  typing the =SCHEDULED:= line and the drawer yourself, or using worg.

=<{{date}} .+1d>= comes out as =<2026-09-30 .+1d>=, with no day name. The
weekday is optional in both org and go-org, and orgs keeps whatever spelling the
line was written with - it moves the date on without adding one. If you want the
day name there, type the whole stamp instead:
=SCHEDULED: {{when|The stamp, e.g. <2026-09-30 Wed .+1d>}}=, at the price of
filling the date in yourself.

** Which repeater to type

The three spellings are three different sums, and the difference only shows on a
habit ticked off late:

| Written  | Means                                                              |
|----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| =.+2d=   | Two days from *today*. What a habit almost always wants: miss a    |
|          | week and the next one is due two days from now, not last Tuesday.  |
| =++2d=   | Two days from the *old date*, repeatedly, until it is in the       |
|          | future. Keeps the rhythm - every other day since you started.      |
| =+2d=    | Two days from the old date, *once*, so it can still be overdue.    |
|          | Right for a deadline, wrong for a habit.                           |

The =/5d= half is org-habit's *slack*: =.+2d/5d= is "every two days, and not
really late until five". A day inside the slack draws as =·= (in hand) rather
than =░= (missed), which is the whole difference between a tracker that reads as
kept and one that reads as failing. There is no reason not to use it on anything
you do not literally do daily.

Times of day work (=SCHEDULED: <2026-09-30 Wed 09:00 .+1d>=) and =.+= keeps the
time when it moves the date on, so a 09:00 reminder ticked off at midnight is
still a 09:00 reminder tomorrow.

** Checking it worked

#+begin_src sh
  orgs listcap                    # the template is loaded
  orgs search 'IsHabit()'         # the heading reads as a habit
  orgs habits                     # it is in the tracker
  orgs habits done 'Morning pages' # tick it - this is what writes the logbook
  orgs habits untick 'Morning pages'
#+end_src

If =orgs search 'IsHabit()'= does not find it, it is the property - the drawer's
column, or the spelling of =:STYLE:=. If it finds it and =orgs habits= shows it
with no squares ever filling, it is the logbook: nothing has ticked it off yet,
or the heading has a =:LOG_INTO_DRAWER:= of its own naming a drawer the
completion reader is not being pointed at.

* What is in each file

- =habits.org= - the main corpus: every repeater spelling (=+2d=, =++2w=, =.+1d=),
  slack halves (=.+3d/5d=, =.+1w/10d=, =.+1m/40d=), a habit with a time of day, a
  kept run, a broken run, a habit never done and overdue, a habit never done and
  not due yet, a habit with no repeater at all, and three repeating-or-dated
  tasks that must *not* read as habits.
- =habits-nodrawer.org= - =#+STARTUP: nologdrawer=, so the =State "DONE"= lines
  are a plain list in the body. Also the double-tick case: twice on one day is
  one day's worth.
- =habits-column-zero.org= - drawers written at column zero. go-org ends the
  headline body there, so =:STYLE: habit= never reaches =Headline.Properties=
  and neither heading reads as a habit. Delete this file if you want a corpus
  where every marked habit is one.

* Expected answers as of <2026-09-29 Tue>

| Heading                            | Schedule       | Streak | Missed |
|------------------------------------+----------------+--------+--------|
| Take vitamins                      | .+1d           |      5 | no     |
| Water the plants                   | .+3d/5d        |      3 | no     |
| Floss                              | .+1d/2d        |      0 | yes    |
| Weekly review                      | .+1w/10d       |      4 | no     |
| Call Mum                           | ++2w           |      3 | no     |
| Change the furnace filter          | .+1m/40d       |      2 | no     |
| Learn guitar scales                | .+1d/3d        |      0 | yes    |
| Start running                      | .+2d/4d        |      0 | no     |
| Morning meds                       | 09:00 .+1d     |      2 | no     |
| Empty the dehumidifier             | +2d            |      0 | yes    |
| Back up the laptop                 | .+1w/9d        |      0 | yes    |
| Water the tomatoes                 | (no repeater)  |      0 | no     |
| Morning pages                      | .+1d/2d        |      3 | no     |
| Stretch                            | .+1d           |      2 | no     |
| Both planning keywords on one line | .+2d           |      0 | no     |

Two of those are the interesting ones. *Change the furnace filter* is 35 days
since its last completion on a monthly habit: over the interval, inside the
slack, so still kept - the case that goes wrong if the interval is used where
the slack should be. *Back up the laptop* has in fact been kept, and reads as
missed because the completion reader asks the *file* which drawer the log lives
in and the habit declares its own =:LOG_INTO_DRAWER: BACKUPS= on the heading.

These numbers are of *today*, so they go stale: a streak that was 5 on the day
this was written is 0 a fortnight later. Shift every date forward, or read the
table as the shape of the answers rather than as the answers.
